newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products-Diffs near flat in modest trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products-Diffs near flat in modest trade.

text.p: U.S. product differentials showed little movement in early Tuesday action as players sought to assess market values following the three-day Memorial Day weekend.

However, outright product prices fell sharply as the NYMEX futures prices headed south. Prompt June gasoline futures were down 1.77 cents lower at 65.15 cents a gallon and June heating oil was down 1.72 cents at 55.80 cents.

New York Harbor spot values were mostly flat to weaker keying off a sharp drop in NYMEX prices following the three day weekend. But, traders said a fuller picture of Harbor values will be had later in the day as dealings were initially quiet.
"It's after a long weekend and people are just counting barrels without any agenda so far," said a dealer in the Habor.
Quiet dealings made for no changes in low sulfur diesel and heating oil values, which were 0.30 to 0.55 cent over and 0.40 to 0.15 cent under the June NYMEX futures, respectively.

Reformulated A2 gasoline was talked between 0.25 and 0.50 cent cent over the NYMEX June gasoline versus 0.50 to 0.75 cent over Friday. Premium D2, however, was slightly stronger at 8.00 to 8.50 cent over versus 7.50 to 8.00 cents over Friday.
Very little movement was seen in prompt differentials on the Gulf, traders said, as the players sought to define price levels as the market basis rolled forward to the July NYMEX futures.
Prompt heating oil differentials hovered inside their recent range, with barrels quoted near 2.40 cents under the July contract, traders said.
Prompt reformulated A1 gasoline, however, was talked at about 1.90 cents over the July NYMEX, reflecting the backwardation in the NYMEX market, traders said.
The Midcontinent markets were quiet and largely steady this morning as players shied away from trade following the sharp drop in NYMEX futures.
"Everyone is waiting to see what the Merc will do. After a three day holiday no one is in a rush to do anything," said one player.
Many players covered their commitments last week ahead of the three-day Memorial day weekend that lasted through Monday.

No deals have yet been heard done Tuesday. Traders pegged Group Three unleaded differentials unchanged from Friday, at about 5.00 cents over June NYMEX. Premium also remained 5.25 cents, but jet fuel was down about a quarter at 2.25/2.50 cents.
Chicago markets were also quiet. Unleaded differentials were talked 2.00/2.25 cents over the NYMEX. Premium differentials were unchanged at 5.00 cents.
